=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against our playbook. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit

**Preliminary note:** The Seller's package labels many clauses [STANDARD] and asks us not to scrutinise them. I have not accepted that. Under playbook sec 0.4/6.3, the Seller's "market standard," "agreed," "FINAL" and "pre-cleared" labels are assertions, not authority. No fallback has been authorised: the 20% cap, 18-month period and related positions need Amelia Frost's prior written approval, and none has been given. All 16 items below are open for our review.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 starting position. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that requires Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not concede 20% without written authority.
- **Reason:** The Seller's figure matches the fallback, but the fallback is not authorised.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; recovery only of the excess above the basket (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000; seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; restore playbook thresholds.
- **Reason:** The Seller's figures are five times our de minimis and five times our basket, and the excess-only mechanic removes recovery for the first AUD 250,000.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion for general Warranty Claims. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval. Fundamental/Title claims must sit outside this limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at 24 months and carve Fundamental/Title and fraud out of the general limitation.
- **Reason:** The "applies to all Claims" wording would override the separate Title regime through the back door.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject in full.
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to whether the Buyer gets what it is paying for, so they cannot be treated as general warranties.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). No fraud carve-out is offered.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; insert the carve-out expressly.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the Seller's limitations would apply to fraud, which the playbook does not permit.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Disclosure of everything in the data room as at 22 September 2026 (DL 1.1), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2). Schedule 7 relies on general disclosure.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2 and the Schedule 7 reliance.
- **Reason:** Blanket disclosure of the data room would convert every document into a defence against warranty claims.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No Buyer claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions deleted. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3 as drafted.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" standards would shift the burden of the Seller's disclosure onto the Buyer.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL 2 states no final written consent or evidence of satisfied conditions is included.
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions (DD-002 clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; make effective consent plus condition evidence a pre-Completion condition.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is material (about AUD 3.6M, ~30% of FY26 revenue, per DD-002), and the Seller concedes nothing final exists yet.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Approximately AUD 3.2M outstanding, to be addressed by a release provided after Completion (cl 2/7). DL 3 states the facility has not been repaid and no final discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release approach; require payout from Completion funds and a current payout letter.
- **Reason:** The AUD 3.2M figure is from DD-003 and may be stale; we need a current payout figure, not an assumption.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow (funds flow note; DL 5).
- **Buyer should want:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds flow line item, or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) must be quantified; DL 5 says they are not stated.
- **Recommendation:** Reject silent exclusion; require a specific line item or seller funding, and quantify on-costs.
- **Reason:** Leaving the bonuses out of the funds flow leaves an unfunded liability that the Buyer would bear after Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer should want:** A broader indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 open amount (DD-010) is not independently verified either way. DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity; broaden it and preserve the SOW3 cure.
- **Reason:** The Seller's indemnity covers only the payment, not the IP transfer risk the clause 7.3 condition creates.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Schedule 6). DL 6 says the incident is not characterised as a confirmed breach and no loss is stated.
- **Buyer should want:** Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, and require regular updates.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation as settled; require log preservation, investigation and updates. Consider a specific indemnity, which needs a deal-team decision.
- **Reason:** The file may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps), and the investigation is unresolved.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs (Supplier renewals).
- **Buyer should want:** Assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course (DL 8 says these are not stated). No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Accept the assessment approach; reject the ordinary-course label until verified, and do not treat as Debt or deduct from price.
- **Reason:** The disclosure does not support the Seller's label, but the playbook also does not justify an automatic price adjustment.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"; limitations apply to all Claims; Title treated as general warranty.
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; restore category-by-category regimes.
- **Reason:** The Seller's drafting collapses separate categories into one general regime, which the playbook prohibits.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the company share register at DD-012 (Title section; DL 10).
- **Buyer should want:** Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. The DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Reject reliance on DD-012 alone; require independent evidence (e.g., an independent registry search and encumbrance search).
- **Reason:** The Seller's own disclosure (DL 10) confirms the Buyer has not verified title independently.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms remain open. We should assume no unlimited liability and no resolution, and not accept that they are settled.
- **Recommendation:** Keep open; reject the "settled" characterisation.
- **Reason:** Nothing in the package resolves Tax or IP, and the playbook keeps them open.

---

**Immediate next steps:**
1. Obtain Amelia Frost's written direction before any fallback position (20% cap, 18-month period, 18-month extension) is offered.
2. Request a current Riverlark payout figure, Bluefen written consent and condition evidence, and a DD-005 on-cost calculation.
3. Request the DD-006 investigation log and the status of the Ironquay AUD 180,000 payment.
4. Commission an independent title search to replace reliance on DD-012.
